reason: Hydrogen nuclei in the core are the star's initial fusion fuel, so combining them with the star is a direct starting point.

choice.with: Hydrogen nuclei in the stellar core

expectation: The star will fuse hydrogen into helium, advancing its interior evolution.

effect: Hydrogen fusion produced a helium-rich core, so the next step is to advance that core's evolution.
reaction: The distinction between the core and a separate object is useful.
reason: Compression in the stellar core should heat the helium-rich core and help initiate its next fusion stage.
expectation: The core will become hot and dense enough for helium fusion.

effect: Compression advanced the core to helium burning; the next available fuel-building step is not yet clear.
reaction: The distinction between stellar temperatures and ordinary chemical heat is useful.

expectation: The inspection will identify an available partner for the next stage of stellar evolution.

alternatives.reason: Helium is the current fuel, but it is unclear whether this separate item represents fuel in the core.

reaction: The triple-alpha explanation clarified how carbon forms from helium.
reason: Further compression may heat the carbon-rich material enough for the next fusion stage.
expectation: Compression will advance the material toward carbon burning.

effect: Compression produced carbon-burning layers, whose reactions make several heavier elements.
reaction: The multiple reaction products are an interesting detail.
reason: Further compression is a plausible way to reach the next, hotter burning stage.
expectation: The layers will advance toward a later stage of stellar fusion.

alternatives.reason: I could check its partners if compression is not the next step.

effect: Compression advanced the star through neon and oxygen burning, producing layers that make silicon and sulfur.

reason: Further compression plausibly brings the core to the next, hotter fusion stage.

effect: Compression brought the star to silicon-burning material, where reactions build toward iron-group nuclei.

reason: Inspecting the oxygen-burning layers may reveal how to assemble the layered interior.

effect: Inspecting the oxygen-burning layers automatically combined them with the carbon-burning layers, completing the layered interior and the chapter.
reaction: The onion metaphor made the coexistence of burning regions clear, though finding the combination took some backtracking.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the onion of burning shells was most worthwhile: it connected the successive fusion stages to regions coexisting within one star, without implying chemically pure shells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The unsuccessful attempt with the iron-group core and the empty inspection of the star were a little frustrating, though they ruled out plausible approaches.

surprise.text: I expected the iron-group core to combine with the star, but it had no available combinations; the layered interior instead came from combining two earlier burning layers.

arbitrary.text: Combining the carbon- and oxygen-burning layers to represent the whole layered interior was not obvious to me, especially after reaching the iron-group core, although the result explains the metaphor.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the explanations of fusion networks and the limits of iron-group fusion made me curious about what happens during core collapse.
